notes.title: New Feature Update: Take Control!
notes.content:
This FREE update adds the long-promised ability to rename CPU drivers and teams, as well as a couple of bonus features such as manual gears and traction control, and a bunch of smaller improvements and fixes. Here is what is included :-

*ADDED The ability to rename CPU drivers and CPU teams. 
*ADDED An option to switch to using manual gears.
*ADDED An option to adjust the amount of traction control the player’s car uses. 
*ADDED An option to give all game characters large eyes. 
*ADDED The ability to skip the tutorial if the player has a saved profile already. 
*IMPROVED Camera occlusion on various tracks when using BLIMP camera view.
*IMPROVED Screen layouts for ultra-wide displays. 
*IMPROVED More intelligent CPU overtaking behaviour.
*FIXED The sound of the engine blowing up on elimination race, does not respect volume settings.
*FIXED Moving from CHAMPIONSHIP to HOT LAP on the Mode Select Screen without moving over CAREER causes the screen scene to offset. 
*FIXED The Caspian Sea time trial loading the wrong track variant. 
*FIXED Game stats appearing in miles when kilometres selected.
*FIXED Starting a race in cockpit view starts the camera inside the character’s head before zooming out. 
*FIXED Track-side speed signs not acting as physics objects.  
*FIXED Season cups readout not displaying correctly.
*FIXED Player’s car sometimes appearing on track instead of in the pits when choosing race strategy.
*FIXED CPU cars sometimes being upside down on track shortly after a race start.
*FIXED The player’s car exiting the pits sometimes starts stationary rather than at pit speed.
*FIXED Incorrect language on the Valencia track run off.
*FIXED New profile saves incorrectly remember the player’s racing line setting.
*FIXED No rewind button in the tutorial when returning from CHAMPIONSHIP MODE. 
*FIXED Changing decades just before a change of globe location could prevent progress. 
*FIXED Phone calls from blank character meshes. 
*FIXED New season title card displaying “season 0” rather than “season 1”.
*FIXED Driver overalls in CHAMPIONSHIP MODE not matching car livery.
*FIXED Audio levels and other settings not saving properly. 
*FIXED Temporary profiles being created when profiles deleted. 

(To change driver or team names, or change the logos of the teams, follow these steps):
1. Go to New Star GP in your Steam Library
2. Click on the cog or right click on the name of the game in the list and select Manage > Browse Local Files
3. The CustomData.txt template file is in the "release" subfolder.
4. Follow the instructions in that file and save the edited version OUTSIDE the "release" subfolder, along with any custom logos you want the game to use. This protects your changes from being overwritten by Steam's file validation.
That’s it!

notes.title: New Star GP review: Putting the fun back in F1
notes.content:
If, right now, you ask a long-time F1 fan what keeps them tuning in to watch cars go round and round while a paddock full of very smart engineers and some of the most dodgy rich people the world has to offer look on, they’ll all probably give different answers.

Some’ll say it’s the drama, some’ll say it’s impressive tech being pushed to the limit, some’ll say they like seeing Charles Leclerc’s pretty face. All of these reasons are equally valid, but, following an opening race to the 2024 season that certainly tested my resolve to tune in again this week - I don’t think many of the answers you got would directly speak to what should be the simple reason any of us watch sports. Above all else, it’s supposed to be fun.

New Star GP, the latest release from the studio behind Retro Bowl and New Star Manager, is exactly that. It’s straight-up fun. Coming out of a recent preview of the game, I honestly wasn’t sure whether it would be, given that it was coming out of early access stocked with a mixture of arcadey and sim-style elements that seemed like they might lead it to struggle to properly deliver enough of either vision.

Read more

notes.title: Welcome to the Year 2000!
notes.content:
NEW DECADE OF RACING, WELCOME TO THE YEAR 2000. 

*ADDED: 2000s racing decade! This CAREER MODE update includes a total of 35 brand new events, and a new racing location in Poland. As if that wasn’t enough, it also adds a grid of new, and more capable CPU drivers and teams to out-race, and 3 new cars for you to upgrade and customise! The two Poland track configurations are also added to CREATE-A-CHAMPIONSHIP MODE, so can be added to your own custom championship configurations. 
*ADDED: Licensed tech! You can now improve your cars not only with upgrades, but also by licensing technology from other teams for temporary performance improvements providing an alternative upgrade strategy, or a temporary boost to beat that hard to finish event. Friendly teams will offer a discount on their tech, but teams driven by hostile drivers will bump the price of theirs!  
*ADDED: Improved news! News has had a graphical update with new staging based on driving decade, plus a selection of new news stories.
*IMPROVED: Higher resolution shadows in cockpit view. 
*IMPROVED: The opportunity to sack an unhappy member of staff! 
*IMPROVED: Edit your character's appearance from the Customise Screen in the garage.
*FIXED: Sound effects now play when you repair a component in the pits. 
*FIXED: Issue with CPU car performance in reverse races not recognising when they’re the lead car.
*FIXED: New stories where CPU drivers were being mis-gendered. 
*FIXED: Quitting championships made in CREATE-A-CHAMPIONSHIP MODE sometimes didn’t save if no return to the Mode Select Screen.   
*FIXED: Dilemma issue in which both staff members increased their happiness. 
*FIXED: Multiplayer championships now save progress between launches, and can be resumed with any number of players.

notes.title: Creation Mode Update
notes.content:
CREATION MODE UPDATE

* ADDED: Create-a-Championship Mode. This mode offers players the ability to create their own custom championship competitions. A host of options are available for tweaking, such as track length, pitting, or weather; and in the advanced options, settings such as race speed, how competitive the CPU opponents are, and the option to carry car damage over between races allows players to customise the experience to their own tastes. The requests for longer race durations have been answered with the option to set race distance (99 lap races anyone?), and to top it off, any custom competitions can be played in either single player, or multiplayer with up to four players.
* ADDED: Staff personalities. Staff now have different personalities: some are easy to keep happy, others less so. Some upset other staff members, others don’t, while some also have special bonus abilities, so choosing between members of staff based on their personalities offers more strategy options for your team and more depth and richness between races. Additionally, staff happiness now offers a bonus to perk performance, so keeping your staff happy is worth the effort as it gains you an edge on the track. 
* ADDED: Some extra staff-related news stories based on their personalities.
* ADDED: A few extra character customisation options.  
* FIXED: Bug where a failure could occur in non-GP races without a warning dilemma.
* FIXED: Title screen crash if more than four controllers are connected. 
* FIXED: Incompatibility problem with save game formats.

notes.title: New Star GP looks like a 3D throwback to the F1 games of the '90s
notes.content:
My purchase last year of a Steam Deck rekindled my long-dormant love for arcade racers. High quality and modern entries in the genre are few and far between, though.

Enter New Star GP, which looks like it might fill the whole in my heart that's been there since I played F1 Pole Position on the SNES in 1993.

Read more

notes.title: This upcoming arcade racing game promises to be a throwback to the '90s in more ways than one
notes.content: I'm not sure I'd go so far as to say that arcade racers are enjoying a renaissance right now, but there's definitely some good stuff to choose from out there, like Circuit Superstars and, more recently, Exo Rally Championship. That number will grow by one later this year with the release of New Star GP, a retro-styled open-wheel racing game set in the heyday of Prost, Senna, and Schumacher... Read more.
